idea: SaludApp Peru: patient uploads prescription photo, OCR extracts data, shows cheapest generic equivalent in nearby pharmacies with real crowdsourced prices, tracks adherence, B2B model selling adherence data to insurers and leads to pharmacies.
market: Peruvian pharmacy retail market worth ~$2B, high out-of-pocket spending, low digital health penetration, fragmented pharmacy chains and independent outlets, growing mobile usage.

solutions.name: Status Quo / Manual Search
solutions.observed_positioning: Patients ask at local pharmacies or call several; accept prices without systematic comparison; no adherence tracking.

solutions.name: Inkafarma App
solutions.observed_positioning: Largest chain, own app with loyalty points, online ordering, and delivery; shows only its own prices, no cross-chain comparison, no adherence features.

solutions.name: Mifarma App
solutions.observed_positioning: Second largest chain, app with e-commerce and promotions; limited to their inventory and prices; no health data integration.

solutions.name: Boticas Arcangel App
solutions.observed_positioning: Growing chain with price-focused positioning; app offers deals and delivery but no adherence or comparative tools.

solutions.name: Farmacias Peruanas App
solutions.observed_positioning: Mid-size chain, basic app for ordering; no price comparison or adherence features.

solutions.name: Rappi Farma
solutions.observed_positioning: Multi-category delivery app with pharmacy section; shows prices from affiliated pharmacies, convenient for comparison within its network, but no adherence or health data analytics.

solutions.name: OPM-DIGEMID
solutions.observed_positioning: Government price observatory; publishes maximum declared prices, no geographical availability, no real-time updates, not user-friendly.

solutions.name: Farmagangas
solutions.observed_positioning: Peruvian website aggregating pharmacy promotions manually; lacks mobile app, OCR, adherence tracking, or real-time data.

solutions.name: Minsa Receta Digital
solutions.observed_positioning: Government digital prescription system, low adoption; could become standard but currently no price or adherence features.

solutions.name: Tarjeta Oh! / Club de Beneficios
solutions.observed_positioning: Loyalty cards offering fixed discounts at partner chains; no price comparison or health tracking.

solutions.name: Farmacias Independientes
solutions.observed_positioning: Small independent pharmacies with variable pricing; no digital presence, manual transactions.

solutions.name: WhatsApp Groups / Redes Sociales
solutions.observed_positioning: Communities sharing recommendations on where to buy cheap medicine; no structured data, unreliable.

solutions.name: Doctoralia / Teleconsultation
solutions.observed_positioning: Online doctor appointments and e-prescriptions; no price comparison or adherence follow-up.

solutions.name: Apps EPS (Rímac, Pacífico)
solutions.observed_positioning: Insurance apps showing coverage and provider networks; no real-time pharmacy pricing or adherence monitoring.

solutions.name: Google Maps / Search
solutions.observed_positioning: Used to find nearby pharmacies and call for prices; manual, time-consuming, no price history or adherence.

research_summary: The market lacks an integrated solution combining real-time geo-specific drug price comparison, adherence tracking, and B2B data monetization. Current alternatives are either single-chain apps (Inkafarma, Mifarma), delivery platforms with limited pharmacy scope (Rappi), government reference lists (OPM-DIGEMID), or rudimentary promotion websites (Farmagangas). No competitor leverages OCR for prescription ingestion, crowdsourced price confirmation, or longitudinal health data. Major threats are well-funded chains that could copy features and Rappi's expansive logistics network. Government platforms pose a long-term regulatory risk if made mandatory.

competitor_signals.sourcing_brief: Largest pharmacy chain in Peru, backed by Intercorp, strong digital presence with over 1M app downloads, high customer loyalty, potential to add competitive features.
Second largest chain, owned by Quicorp, app with basic e-commerce, strong offline presence, could invest in digital.
Multi-billion dollar unicorn with presence across Latin America, including Peru. Aggressive expansion in pharmacy delivery and digital services; could easily add price comparison.
Peruvian website that compares pharmacy prices manually, low traffic, no mobile app, limited to promotional offers, no health data angle.
Official drug price observatory by DIGEMID, publishes maximum prices but lacks real-time data, geographic availability, or user-friendly interface. Potential to become mandatory reference.
